title: What is Sales Velocity and How Does it Impact Your Partner Programs?
summary: In this article, we share how to calculate and optimize sales velocity to enhance partnership performance and drive growth.
body_markdown:
Which quality is better for a sales team: speed or quality? As the kid in the old Taco Bell commercial goes: why not both?


Sales velocity measures how quickly good deals move through your pipeline and turn into revenue. To calculate it, multiply your number of opportunities, average deal size and win rate, then divide by your sales cycle length. Partners can raise it by showing buyers how your product fits their needs and helping your team close deals faster.


The metric helps sales teams balance both speed and quality while staying focused on their day-to-day sales motions.


Sales velocity helps answer two important questions when it comes to the overall sales function. Are we moving in the right direction? And are we moving fast enough?


**In this article, we spoke with Zak Pines, VP of Partnerships at Intellistack (formerly Formstack), to discuss:**


- **What is sales velocity?**
- **Why are partnership programs so important for sales velocity?**
- **How can teams improve it to increase revenue?**


## What is sales velocity?


Sales velocity is the pace at which high-quality deals advance.


To really understand this, you have to understand the difference between speed and velocity. Don’t worry — we’ll keep the physics talk quick and simple.


Speed is just how quickly something moves over a distance. Velocity is how quickly something moves over a distance in a specific direction. This is why it’s called “sales velocity” and not “sales speed.”


Good businesses aren’t just trying to get money through the door by any means necessary. They’re trying to grow by building *quality* relationships with customers in the market and solving a *real need* . This helps their business go the distance.


Let’s assume you sell accounting software for eCommerce businesses. Your goal is to become the most trusted accounting software in North America that helps your customers manage everything from their cash flow to creating projections.


If you were measuring sales speed, you’d just be seeing how much money is coming through the door. You wouldn’t care if your customers were enjoying real value from your product or staying happy over the long term, but as a result, you wouldn’t reach that end goal of being the most trusted accounting software that owns the bulk of market share.


“Speed is important, but it has to be quality touches as well,” Pines explains. “That’s the balance you need to strike when engaging and developing opportunities. A combination of the right velocity along with quality interactions with your prospect or customer.”


Good news: there’s a simple formula for measuring sales velocity, and its deal size and win rate inputs reflect the “quality interactions” Pines mentions. The formula is:


**sales velocity = (number of opportunities x average deal size x win rate) ÷ sales cycle length**


Note: if you sell subscriptions, you can swap in average customer lifetime value for average deal size.


Here’s an illustrative example. Say you have 100 sales opportunities, an average deal size of $20K, a 25 per cent win rate and a 90-day sales cycle:


**sales velocity = (100 x $20K x 25%) ÷ 90**


This equals a sales velocity of about $5,556 in revenue per day.


If partners help shorten that cycle to 60 days and nothing else changes:


**sales velocity = (100 x $20K x 25%) ÷ 60**


This equals a sales velocity of about $8,333 in revenue per day — an increase of 50 per cent.


## How does sales velocity relate to partner programs?


Sales velocity and partner programs reinforce each other: strong velocity makes your products more attractive to partners, and partners can help raise it. Just because a company joins your partner program doesn’t mean its sales team will prioritize your products. On the other hand, if you can demonstrate that you have high sales velocity, there’s more incentive for sales teams — who want to win as many high-quality deals as possible — to prioritize your solutions as a[co-selling](https://partnerstack.com/articles/what-is-coselling-in-a-partner-ecosystem) opportunity during conversations with customers.


Understanding sales velocity can also help your partner program gain more respect. Since sales velocity is an important metric for sales and revenue leaders, it’s a good idea to understand how partner programs contribute positively to it.


“If you can show that[partners are helping you close deals more quickly](https://partnerstack.com/articles/how-partner-sales-alignment-can-supercharge-performance) , that is a key metric for any sales manager and sales leader. Most benchmarks show that a partner-generated or partner-attached pipeline is the highest performing pipeline that a business can generate and this is crucial for how you most efficiently grow your business through partnerships,” explains Pines.


One benchmark that supports this point: in Pavilion and Ebsta’s Spring 2024 B2B Sales Benchmarks, as[outlined in our Research Lab](https://partnerstack.com/resources/research-lab/charts/partner-driven-represents-highest-revenue-source-for-top-performing-sales-reps) , partner referrals were only 10 per cent of pipeline — but 31 per cent of revenue.


Here are some examples of the positive relationship between sales velocity and partner programs.


### How do partners accelerate revenue generation?


Partner-generated or partner-attached sales opportunities inject more value into the sales process. Customers gain insight into how a solution can be implemented or how a solution can be customized to their specific industry or use case, something a vendor alone may be unable to provide.


This value accelerates revenue generation by speeding up the sales process without compromising on quality or relationship building. For example,[HubSpot](https://partnerstack.com/integrations/hubspot) can sell you its software and help with technical issues, but an agency in its partner network might be better able to understand the customers’ needs and tailor their pitch accordingly.


PartnerStack and Wynter’s research points the same way.[In The State of Partnerships in GTM 2026 report](https://partnerstack.com/resources/research-lab/charts/partnerships-lead-to-higher-average-contracts-through-larger-initial-deals-upsells-and-renewels) , 48 per cent of teams with strong alignment between partnerships and other go-to-market teams saw shorter sales cycles, and 23 per cent landed bigger deals. That maps to two of the formula’s inputs: sales cycle length and average deal size.


Fundraise Up offers a concrete example. In 2023, its partner-sourced deals closed at a rate of almost 60 per cent, nearly three times the rate of its other acquisition channels, with contract values about 30 per cent larger than its direct sales motion and deals closing about 20 per cent faster, according to[PartnerStack’s Fundraise Up case study](https://partnerstack.com/customers/fundraise-up) . Even though partner-sourced deals take more effort to set up, “it’s still closing faster,” says Salvatore Salpietro, who was Chief Community Officer at Fundraise Up at the time.


### How does high sales velocity improve partner engagement?


High sales velocity points to a smooth sales process. Sales teams within partner organizations want to focus on products and services that are likely to generate revenue. These programs usually have clear-cut solutions as well as[enablement materials](https://partnerstack.com/glossary/enablement-materials) , such as marketing materials and certification courses. Demonstrating that you have high sales velocity shows that you’re selling something worth people’s time.


You can even track correlations between changes in your sales velocity and changes in your[partner KPIs](https://partnerstack.com/glossary/partner-kpi) , particularly those that measure partner engagement. Examples of partner engagement KPIs include per-partner revenue, partner satisfaction scores, partner portal usage rates, lead response time and training or certification completion rates.


### How does sales velocity improve market competitiveness?


An increase in a company’s sales velocity can also lead to an increase in its competitiveness. The faster a company can get customers paying for its products and services, the more market share it can gobble up. Acquiring more customers also means more opportunities to build deep long-term relationships. These relationships can help companies learn about the intricacies of different industries and use cases, generate case studies, cross-sell and upsell and even[co-create new integrations](https://partnerstack.com/articles/how-to-prioritize-integration-partners) .

## What are the key components of sales velocity?


Sales velocity has four key components: the number of opportunities, average deal size, win rate and sales cycle length. It’s important to respect each of these components in order to get a sales process that’s not only fast, but helps you work towards your business goals in a sustainable way as well.


### Number of opportunities


How many opportunities are coming through the door? It’s important that there is sufficient pipeline and that those opportunities are managed in a consistent and efficient way. A low number of opportunities may mean that you need to increase or improve your marketing materials, place more cold calls and send more cold emails. Partners can add to your pipeline too, by sending you qualified introductions.


### Average deal size (or customer lifetime value)


If sales velocity were just about how quickly you could get people to sign on the dotted line, it wouldn’t be a high-quality metric. Velocity implies direction and your business wants to move in the direction of growth and quality relationships. Average deal size or, for subscription-based businesses,[average customer lifetime value](https://partnerstack.com/glossary/life-time-revenue-aka-customer-lifetime-value-or-cltv) , indicates how much business customers are willing to hand over to you.


There are several ways that you can improve average deal size, or lifetime customer value if you’re selling a subscription-based product:


- **Focus on the value that you deliver instead of the cost.** When you understand a customer’s pain points and then link your solution to those pain points, you can charge a higher price point.
- **Make your unique**[value proposition](https://partnerstack.com/glossary/value-proposition) **clear.** Furthermore, it’s helpful to qualify your leads to ensure you’re focusing your energy in the right places. One framework you can use is MEDDIC, which stands for Metrics, Economic Buyer, Decision Criteria, Decision Process, Identify Pain and Champion.
- **Create customer success materials that help your customers get more out of your products and services.** While this may seem more important for subscription-based businesses, it’s also important for other businesses since focusing on post-sale success can lead to more upsell and cross-sell opportunities.


### Win rate


Naturally, win rate has a direct effect on sales velocity. The higher the share of opportunities you win, the higher your sales velocity. There are a few ways you can improve your win rate, including nurturing your leads throughout the sales funnel, aligning your sales process (for example, through demos and emails) to the customer’s specific pain points and needs and deepening your relationships with your existing clients — since a new sale with an existing customer is still a win.


“Sales velocity speaks to how effectively you engage prospects and align to helping them solve problems and the value of your product,” says Pines. “So I think the more effectively you do that as a business, the more effectively you do that with partners. That sets you up to be more competitive in the market. You’re basically outselling your competition at that point and you are winning in your market.”


### Sales cycle length


Sales cycle length is how long it takes to close a deal, and it’s what you divide by in the formula. Shorter sales cycles mean higher velocity: in the example above, going from 90 days to 60 days raised it by 50 per cent. A documented sales process, early lead qualification and partners joining calls or demos can help.

## What are some strategies to improve sales velocity?


You can improve sales velocity by working on any of its four inputs: getting more opportunities, landing bigger deals, winning a higher share of them or shortening the sales cycle. The steps below focus on your sales process, which touches all four.


### How do you optimize your sales process?


Optimizing your sales process is one of the most effective ways to improve sales velocity.


#### How do you map your existing sales processes?


A sales process is a set of repeatable steps. Often, a company’s sales function operates with a set of informal activities that everyone knows they’re supposed to do. A proper sales process is documented and it’s something that you can learn even if you aren’t an early employee or an experienced sales whiz. Mapping out your sales process helps your leadership team evaluate the process, compare results at different periods and make adjustments in a measurable, controlled way.


It’s time to take your sales process from informal to formal by clearly documenting it. You’ll certainly find a few of these steps in your current activities. Keep in mind that some of the earlier steps in the sales process may overlap with your marketing team’s activities.


- Prospecting, cold calling and lead generation
- Lead scoring and lead qualification
- Lead nurturing
- Discovery calls
- Demos
- Stakeholder conversations (particularly for complex implementations)
- Implementation


#### What sales KPIs should you track?


When you’re improving your sales process, it’s important to map out the[key performance indicators (KPIs)](https://partnerstack.com/articles/partner-program-kpis-metrics-you-should-measure-and-optimize) your team will be obsessive about tracking.


Examples of important sales KPIs include:


- Monthly calls or emails per sales rep
- Number of monthly discovery calls
- Number of monthly demos
- Number of closed deals
- Average cost per lead
- Customer lifetime value
- Win rate
- Average sales cycle length
- Partner-sourced revenue


There are all kinds of sales KPIs that you can track. It’s important to track those that are most important to you. Too many KPIs can be overwhelming and as a result, people may stop paying attention to them.


#### How can automation simplify sales activities and KPI tracking?


Technology can help improve your sales process through organization and automation. For instance, a customer relationship management tool such as Salesforce or HubSpot can help you keep all of your contacts in one place, track your different interactions and conversations with them and automate certain activities such as sending out sales emails. You can also[integrate your CRM with your PartnerStack PRM](https://partnerstack.com/platform/partner-tracking) to host all the data you need in one place.

## How does a partner program contribute to sales velocity in practice?


As VP of Partnerships at Intellistack (formerly Formstack), Pines has seen firsthand how a partner program can increase a company’s sales velocity. He shared how Formstack, which is a Salesforce partner, landed a customer in by leveraging its partner relationship.


“If I’m a Formstack rep working an opportunity, our partner manager working with Salesforce can help us get to the Salesforce account executive on that opportunity,” explains Pines. “We can get insights on the buying team, how that customer likes to buy. So the insights will then help the Formstack rep sell more effectively and close or advance that deal faster, having that positive impact on sales velocity.”


Pines says that this is not something that they leave to chance. Whenever they have a new opportunity, they actively look to their partner community, which includes a large community of system integrators (SIs) to find existing relationships.


“We use a product called Reveal to see if there are existing partner relationships on an account that can help us improve sales velocity. And also if a customer has a specific use case where a partner is specialized, we’ll bring that partner in for the credibility and the experience they have around the problem that that customer is trying to solve.”


*(Editor’s note: Reveal has since merged with Crossbeam. For a primer on how these tools work, see our*[guide to account mapping](https://partnerstack.com/articles/account-mapping) *.)*


Pines also points out that it’s not just a matter of leveraging your partner program to win but promoting the impact of your partner program on sales velocity as well.


“The best way is to socialize success and have peer-to-peer sharing,” says Pines. “That’s very valuable. Whenever we have wins, we’ll share that out in Slack channels. We have a way to congratulate people for their contributions. In things like sales standups or internal enablement sessions, we have salespeople share those successes with others.”


“There could be a team member who has done a Formstack project, implemented Formstack, helped the customer achieve value for their data collection or document automation use cases. And we’ll encourage team members to share that success story across their colleagues, so others can learn about what we’ve done together and how we’ve helped a joint customer.”

## Sales velocity FAQs


### What’s the difference between sales velocity and sales speed?


Sales speed measures how quickly you bring in money. Sales velocity also considers the quality of your deals. It shows how fast strong deals move through your pipeline, not just how quickly you close any deal.


### How do you calculate sales velocity?


To calculate sales velocity, multiply your number of opportunities by your average deal size and win rate. Then divide that result by the length of your sales cycle. For example, 100 opportunities times $20K times 25 per cent, divided by 90 days, equals about $5,556 in revenue per day.


### How do partners affect sales velocity?


Partners can give you qualified introductions, help you close bigger deals and make your sales cycles shorter, especially when your partnerships and sales teams are aligned.
